To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the application of diverse organic fertilizers to tomato plants did not influence the structure and diversity of rhizosphere and blossom and fruit bacterial communities; and 2) the structure of the tomato rhizosphere microbiome was more influenced by edaphic factors, such as soil texture, than the application of diverse fertilizer types.
tomato plant organs, including blossoms and fruit, support diverse bacterial communities that are influenced by soil characteristics and plant anatomy, but not by diverse soil amendments.
the tomato microbiome, as assessed by 16S amplicon sequencing, was not significantly impacted by application of various organic and synthetic fertilizer types.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the impact of agricultural practices on the tomato phytobiome, and how this information may contribute to a more comprehensive understanding on the impact of agricultural management practices on plant health and food safety.
the influence of agricultural practice on the structure and diversity of the tomato phyllosphere microbiome, which is an important aspect of the tomato phytobiome.
how plant-associated bacterial communities respond to the application of organic fertilizers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tomato microbiome is more influenced by plant and field characteristics than by the type of soil amendment used.

the application of microbiologically diverse fertilizers had little effect on tomato phytobiome diversity or structure, and that the plant anatomy and field location were more important determinants of the bacterial communities associating to tomato plants.
the tomato phytobiome, including both the phyllosphere as well as the rhizosphere communities, was not significantly influenced by the use of diverse fertilizers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tomato plant is a robust ecosystem and that the phyllosphere is an important reservoir for the rhizosphere microbiome.
soil amendments did not significantly alter the tomato microbiome, but that the plant organ microbiome is influenced by soil and air characteristics.

tomato plants are able to maintain a stable and diverse microbiome in the presence of diverse soil amendments, and that the microbiome of tomato plants is more sensitive to environmental conditions than to the application of diverse soil amendments.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the tomato plant microbiome is not easily manipulated by organic or synthetic fertilizer amendments, suggesting that the microbiome is more likely to be shaped by the plant genotype, the environment and the plant's developmental stage.
the use of organic amendments in tomato production does not have an adverse effect on plant-associated bacterial communities, and therefore, may not pose a risk to plant health and food safety.
, in the absence of disease, the tomato plant is able to tolerate the application of diverse soil amendments, and maintain its phytobiome.
